body.statement: Conditional on D0 validating the candidate frontier, what is the exact order \(\mathcal R_n(d;B,c)\), up to constants depending only on \(B\) and \(c\), of \(K_n(d;B,c)\) throughout the resulting Gaussian regime; in particular, can legal CGD graph-and-endpoint arrays match each dominant verified martingale error term?
body.justification: This secondary question is conditional: the degree frontier and its internal rate bound must first survive the answer-open D0 audit.
body.gap: Exactness in \cite{Haeusler1988MartingaleRate} ranges over general martingales, and optimality in \cite{JanischLehericy2024SparseDependencyGraph} ranges over general dependency graphs; neither proves attainability by CGD arrays.
body.consumer: A matched rate would quantify how conservative the asymptotic degree rule is at the finite graph sizes used in experiment planning.

obligation.what_is_open: The exact constant-order expression for \(\mathcal R_n(d;B,c)\) when \(d=o(n^{2/3})\), including a legal CGD lower array matching each dominant normal-approximation term.
obligation.obstruction: The verified Heyde--Brown bound has the generic martingale exponent \(1/5\), but its known sharpness examples are not shown to be representable by the constrained CGD prefix-product increments.  The repeated-star family proves a non-Gaussian critical boundary but does not match the vanishing \(1/5\)-power upper rate in the subcritical regime.
obligation.attempted: The forward Doob decomposition, the shared-parent flip envelope, the spectral operator chain, and the repeated-star hub-count perturbation were all derived.  They close the convergence frontier, but no CGD endpoint and graph array obtained from these constructions matches the generic martingale rate throughout the interior regime.
obligation.partial_result:
The verified results give the uniform upper bound
\[
 K_n(d;B,c)\le \min\left\{1,C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)
 \left(d^{3/2}/n\right)^{1/5}\right\}
\]
throughout the Gaussian regime \(d=o(n^{2/3})\).  At every fixed critical scale \(d_n\ge \beta n^{2/3}+o(n^{2/3})\), the repeated-star construction gives
\[
 \liminf_nK_n(d_n;B,c)\ge
 d_{\mathrm K}(\mathcal L_\beta,\mathcal N(0,1))>0.
\]
These conclusions determine the sharp convergence frontier but do not determine the exact vanishing order inside that frontier.
